363	The Torah simply repeats itself from beginning to end.

364	Parashiot Terumah, Tetzaveh: the Torah commands about

365	the Mishkan, two and a half Torah portions. It commands about

366	the Mishkan. This week the Torah tells one thing: they did

367	exactly what was commanded, one for one. The Torah goes through, compare:

368	Terumah, Tetzaveh, what they were commanded there, here they did. Everyone

369	who reads this wonders: why? Why 200 verses?

370	Every letter in the Torah is precise. Every crown on

371	the letters is precise. After all, many of the disputes in the Jewish people

372	stem from the fact that the Torah

373	is brief in its wording. The Torah doesn't say tefillin. Each

374	one of us buys tefillin for a thousand shekels, for 1,000

375	dollars. What does the Torah say about tefillin?

376	"And they shall be for totafot between your eyes." That is all

377	the Torah says: "Bind them as a sign on your hand, totafot

378	between your eyes." Not the color of the tefillin, not the shape of

379	the tefillin, not how to write them, not what to

380	write them on. The Torah is brief in its wording. All the laws of

381	shechitah, such difficult laws: "and you shall slaughter" is one phrase. From it

382	the Sages learned, passing it down in the tradition. The Torah doesn't speak

383	too much. The Torah is sparing with kinds,

384	sparing with words. Suddenly we reach Parashat Vayakhel-

385	Pekudei: the Torah speaks and speaks and speaks and speaks

386	of things that seemingly have no meaning, no

387	importance. They wouldn't have been written; everything would be the same if

388	these two parashiot were missing. The Torah could have

389	written one verse: "Moshe assembled the entire congregation of

390	the children of Israel and told them to build a Mishkan, and they did

391	all that they were commanded," and we would understand that all is well.

392	Why does the Torah repeat in Parashiot Vayakhel-Pekudei? So

393	we have said several times a simple and

394	obvious point: sometimes HaShem speaks about

395	something. When? When He loves it. When He loves

396	the subject. When something moving happens, then HaShem

397	speaks about it. And what happened in these parashiot? People

398	gave money. What is more moving than people who overcome

399	their stinginess, overcome their ego,

400	and open their wallets? Moshe asked for money

401	for the Mishkan. Parashat Vayakhel describes a frenzy of giving

402	that has no equal in the entire Torah. People run: "And they brought

403	him still more freewill offerings, morning by morning." What is "morning,

404	morning"? Twice, "morning." The Kli Yakar says: first, they

405	did not wait to be asked; they simply ran and gave

406	in the morning. Second, the Kli Yakar says something very beautiful.

407	He says: know that if you want to know whether a person

408	does something willingly or unwillingly: you asked

409	a person for a loan. How do you know whether he is just

410	waiting for you to hang up and sort it out on your own, or whether he

411	truly wants to give you? Look at his answer.

412	If he tells you, "Call me tomorrow morning,"

413	know that he is preparing the money; he goes to the bank tonight,

414	he prepares the cash for you. If he

415	tells you, "Talk to me in the evening," know that he hopes

416	you will sort it out. "And they brought him still more freewill offerings, morning,

417	morning." In the morning we do what we love; in the evening we do

418	what we have no choice about, what we can no longer put off.

419	The Torah says "morning" twice because they wanted to give.

420	They gave with such enthusiasm that, as the parashah tells,

421	they had to close the collection boxes. How?

422	Moshe says: "Enough!" Stop

423	bringing money. This is the only fundraiser in history

424	that ended with people coming and saying, "Don't bring any more." There is no

425	money in the bank; the bank said there is no more money, don't bring.

426	There is no room to put it. People gave and poured out freewill offerings,

427	a giving like never before in history. So

428	how do you compare this? On one side, Moshe has

429	time; he keeps the good news in his belly and gives it

430	only the next morning. And the Jewish people, what a burst of

431	giving, what a burst of offerings, what a burst of fundraising,

432	so much that HaShem does not stop speaking

433	about it and repeats it and repeats it. Let us read:

462	how do we reconcile, how do we support, on one side the alacrity of

463	the people of Israel, and on the other side the supposed procrastination of Moshe,

464	who postpones the news of building the Mishkan until the day after

465	Yom Kippur? What is the point here? Because there is another beautiful thing:

466	it is not only that they give; they do something far

467	greater than giving. There is something harder than

468	giving money. Giving money is the easiest thing in life. There is

469	something harder: giving time. Many people

470	are willing to give money, but leave me alone, to give

471	your hands and your feet, to give time and devote

472	yourself to the work, to come yourself to help arrange

473	the synagogue, to clean the synagogue, and to sort out

474	the synagogue's accounts: that is the truly hard thing.

475	The great wonder in Parashiot Vayakhel-Pekudei is that they don't only

476	give money, they give time. Everyone who knew: "all the wise-hearted," every person

477	who knew how to do something, to weave,
